description: The scenes and levels of a Game Kit project (gkp_…), game.engine 1.7 — use this tool, never code a scene manager. A scene has a kind: interface (no world: title, main menu, credits — kits build nothing, the renderers draw no world), 2d, 3d (default), loading (shown while the next scene loads), cinematic; a role: menu (entered first, Play leads on), level (levels follow the order), credits, other; next (the scene that follows: Play from the menu, the end of a level, the script verb next_scene); loading (how it shows when its files are not ready — on demand: preloaded or cached files go straight in, a screen comes up only after sceneFlow.showAfterMs; overlay = ui.menu's loading screen with the real asset.preload progress, none, background = the scene left stays until this one is ready, or a scene id: a loading scene or an interface scene of the game); loadingScreen { image, tips, background, title } (several screens per game: one per scene, or flow.loadingScreen); background { image, video, color, scene } of an interface scene; unload (release | keep); transition (replace: the scene left is unloaded | add: it stays loaded under this one) and below (what the scenes under an added scene do: run, pause = drawn but frozen, hide = not drawn). Scenes stack and keep their states at run time — the game changes scene by program (engine.scenes.enter(scene, entry, { unload: false, previous: { visible, paused } }), push / pop / unload / activate / set(scene, { visible, paused }); script verbs load_scene { unload: false }, push_scene, pop_scene, set_scene): a scene kept loaded is frozen in memory and resumed at once; nothing a loaded scene uses is freed. The flow (game.engine config sceneFlow): transition replace | add, menu scene | overlay (scene: the title of ui.menu is a scene of its own, entered first with no world behind it — synthesised as menu when the project writes none; every new game and every opened game has it), menuScene, loading overlay | scene | none | background, loadingScene, showAfterMs, minLoadingMs, loadTimeout (s), onFail retry | enter | wait, retries, loadingScreen, unload. Each scene loads its files before it is entered (asset.preload, progress on the loading screen) and leaving it frees its instances and the memory of the files only it used (never the disk cache); hooks engine.scene.change (redirect or refuse a change) and engine.scene.release, events engine.scene.loading / loaded / unloaded / refused for mods. The asset list of a scene (scene_assets: files with role, phase, size, shared) is generated from its content (instances → archetype models, the global slots a played scene needs, world, HUD, music, menu art) — retouch it by hand or with assets_put; asset.preload uses it as one more source, never a restriction. action=list (default; scene: one scene with its files and plan): the flow (menu, start, levels, loading), each scene (kind, role, next, instances, world kit, files, written or generated list), the scene issues of the report, the check of the asset lists and the load plan (per scene in play order: what entering it loads, what leaving it frees, what is shared, and the loading screen of that transition). action=create { id, kind?, role?, title?, next?, loading?, background?, world?, at? (index) } | update { id, set: {…} } (null clears a key) | remove { id } | order { ids } (these first, in this order) | link { id, next } (next null: unlink) | flow { set: { menu, menuScene, transition, loading, loadingScene, showAfterMs, minLoadingMs, loadTimeout, onFail, retries, loadingScreen, unload } } | menu { id?, title?, background? } (writes the menu scene as a document, first, role menu) | assets { scene? } (generate or refresh the lists; files written by hand are kept) | assets_put { scene, files } | assets_check (missing file, file used by nothing, duplicate, list out of date). dry_run answers the new state without writing. Every write answers the new state. Scene content (instances, entries, zones, scripts) stays with gripforge_game_content. 0 credits.

action.description: list (default) | create | update | remove | order | link | flow | menu | assets | assets_put | assets_check.

at.description: create: its index in the order of the scenes.

background.description: create, menu: { image?, video?, color?, scene? } of an interface scene.

dry_run.description: Every write: answer the new state without writing.

files.description: assets_put: the files of the scene ({ id, slot? | path?, role, phase?, bytes?, shared? }; source manual by default).

id.description: create, update, remove, link, menu: the scene id.

ids.description: order: the scenes first, in this order.

kind.description: create: the kind of the scene (default 3d).

loading.description: create: a loading scene id, overlay or none.

next.description: create, link: the scene that follows (link: null unlinks).

project_id.description: Game Kit project id (gkp_…). Not a dedicated-server project (gpj_…) nor a Library item.

role.description: create: its part in the game.

scene.description: list: one scene (its files and plan); assets, assets_put: the scene.

set.description: update: the scene keys to change; flow: the sceneFlow keys.

title.description: create, menu: the title (an i18n.text key preferably).

workspace_id.description: Workspace authorized by the current key. Never infer another user’s workspace.

world.description: create: { kit, config?, doc? } the world kit of a 3d / 2d scene.
